[open] Issue #835: [P2] getSemantic RLock without proactive eviction — stale entries accumulate silently
  Author: @anchapin
  Status: OPEN
  URL: https://github.com/anchapin/nexus-proxy/issues/835

  Description:
    **Focus area**: Routing Intelligence
    **PRD phase**: Phase 5 — Intelligence/DX
    **Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
    **Labels**: `enhancement`, `area:router`, `phase:5-intelligence`
    
    ### Problem
    `getSemantic` at `slm_cache.go:274` acquires `c.mu.RLock()` and scans all live `c.entries` for cosine similarity. Expired entries are skipped for similarity scoring (`now.Sub(entry.stamp) > c.ttl → continue`) but are **never removed** from `c.entries` or `c.expiry`. Since `getSemantic` holds an RLock (readers don't block readers), it cannot call `evictExpired` (which needs a write lock). With low request volume and long TTL, expired entries accumulate indefinitely between `Set` calls. `Stats().Expired` reports them but no metric surfaces this as a Prometheus gauge.
    
    ### Proposed solution
    Add `Stale()` method to `SLMCache` returning count of expired-but-live entries. In `getSemantic`, if `Stale() > 0` after the scan, dispatch a background eviction signal. Also expose `nexus_slm_cache_stale_entries` gauge in `routemetrics.go`.
    
    ### Acceptance criteria
    - [ ] `SLMCache.Stale()` returns count of expired-but-not-yet-evicted entries
    - [ ] After TTL expiry on a semantic-cache entry, `Stale()` increases by 1 and `/metrics` reflects it
    - [ ] `getSemantic` with `NEXUS_SLMCACHE_MAX_STALE=1` triggers proactive eviction on next `Get`/`getSemantic` call
    - [ ] Unit test: insert 3 entries, wait past TTL, verify `Stale() == 3` and no eviction yet
    - [ ] `make test-race` passes
    
    ### References
    - `internal/router/slm_cache.go:274-313` — `getSemantic`
    - `internal/router/slm_cache.go:184-206` — `evictExpired` (write-lock only)
    - `internal/router/slm_cache.go:458-476` — `Stats()` which already computes `Expired`

14: // `nexus_slm_cache_evictions_total{reason=...}` series (issue #449).

23: // Embedder turns text into a vector for semantic similarity comparison.
24: // It is safe for concurrent use.

26: 	Embed(ctx context.Context, text string) ([]float64, error)
27: }

29: // SLMCache is a time-bounded prompt → route cache (issue #206). It
30: // deduplicates identical prompts within a TTL window so repeated
31: // identical requests (e.g. the same task retried) do not trigger an
32: // SLM call. This reduces SLM latency and cost for bursty duplicate
33: // traffic.
34: //
35: // When an Embedder is configured (issue #245), the cache also performs
36: // semantic deduplication: prompts whose embedding cosine similarity
37: // exceeds the configured threshold are treated as cache hits even when
38: // the exact string differs. For example, "write a fibonacci function"
39: // and "implement fibonacci recursively" would share the same cached
40: // route decision.
41: //
42: // The cache is safe for concurrent use. It uses a sync.RWMutex so
43: // readers (cache lookups) do not block each other; writers (cache
44: // inserts) take an exclusive lock.
45: //
46: // Eviction counters (issue #449): TTL and LRU removals each bump an
47: // atomic counter that is exposed via Stats() and forwarded to a
48: // caller-supplied eviction observer so the proxy can distinguish
49: // "TTL too short" (high churn) from "cache undersized" (capacity
50: // pressure) in /metrics as `nexus_slm_cache_evictions_total{reason}`.
51: //
52: // Zero value is ready to use with default TTL (DefaultSLMCacheTTL).
53: // Construct with NewSLMCache to override TTL.
54: type SLMCache struct {
55: 	ttl          time.Duration
56: 	maxEntries   int
57: 	embedder     Embedder
58: 	semThreshold float64 // cosine similarity floor for semantic match (0.0..1.0)
59: 
60: 	mu      sync.RWMutex
61: 	entries map[string]cachedDecision
62: 	expiry  []string // keys sorted by expiry time (earliest first)
63: 
64: 	// ttlEvictions and lruEvictions are cumulative atomic counters
65: 	// bumped inside the synchronized eviction paths so they are safe
66: 	// to read concurrently with Set (issue #449). They are not
67: 	// guarded by mu because the hot path already holds it; atomic
68: 	// updates keep Stats() lock-free.
69: 	ttlEvictions uint64
70: 	lruEvictions uint64

73: 	// embedder call in Set and getSemantic when the embedder returns

75: 	embedErrors uint64

78: 	// with reason = "ttl" or "lru". The callback runs AFTER the

80: 	// or any other subsystem without risking re-entrant deadlocks.

101: // DefaultSLMCacheTTL is the default cache entry lifetime. 30 seconds
102: // covers the typical burst window where a coding agent retries the
103: // same prompt. Operators can override via NewSLMCache(ttl).
104: const DefaultSLMCacheTTL = 30 * time.Second

106: // DefaultSLMCacheMaxEntries is the default max entries cap. 512 covers
107: // a typical burst of distinct prompts without excessive memory use.
108: const DefaultSLMCacheMaxEntries = 512

110: // DefaultSemanticThreshold is the default cosine similarity floor for
111: // semantic cache hits (issue #245). 0.85 is a conservative threshold
112: // that groups very similar prompts (same intent, different wording)
113: // without false positives.

116: // NewSLMCache constructs a cache with the given TTL and max entries.
117: // Pass zero TTL to use DefaultSLMCacheTTL; zero maxEntries to use
118: // DefaultSLMCacheMaxEntries. The returned cache has semantic
119: // deduplication disabled; use NewSLMCacheWithEmbedder to enable it.
120: func NewSLMCache(ttl time.Duration, maxEntries int) *SLMCache {

123: 	}

131: 		semThreshold: DefaultSemanticThreshold,
132: 	}
133: }

135: // NewSLMCacheWithEmbedder constructs a cache with the given TTL, max
136: // entries, and semantic deduplication enabled. embedder is used to
137: // compute prompt embeddings; threshold is the cosine similarity floor
138: // (0.0..1.0) for two prompts to be considered semantically equivalent.
139: // Pass zero threshold to use DefaultSemanticThreshold.
140: func NewSLMCacheWithEmbedder(ttl time.Duration, maxEntries int, embedder Embedder, threshold float64) *SLMCache {
141: 	if ttl <= 0 {
142: 		ttl = DefaultSLMCacheTTL
143: 	}
144: 	if maxEntries <= 0 {
145: 		maxEntries = DefaultSLMCacheMaxEntries
146: 	}
147: 	if threshold <= 0 {
148: 		threshold = DefaultSemanticThreshold
149: 	}
150: 	return &SLMCache{
151: 		ttl:          ttl,
152: 		maxEntries:   maxEntries,
153: 		embedder:     embedder,
154: 		semThreshold: threshold,
155: 		entries:      make(map[string]cachedDecision),
156: 	}

159: // sortExpiry sorts the expiry slice by stamp (earliest first).
160: // This maintains the invariant that expiry[0] is the entry to evict next.
161: // Orphaned entries (present in c.expiry but deleted from c.entries) are
162: // sorted first by treating their stamp as the epoch (time.Time{}) so they
163: // are always candidates for immediate eviction.
164: func (c *SLMCache) sortExpiry() {
165: 	sort.Slice(c.expiry, func(i, j int) bool {
166: 		iEntry, oki := c.entries[c.expiry[i]]
167: 		jEntry, okj := c.entries[c.expiry[j]]
168: 		if !oki {
169: 			// Orphaned i sorts before valid j; two orphans use zero time
170: 			// (consistent, sorts to front of any valid entry).
171: 			return true
172: 		}
173: 		if !okj {
174: 			return false
175: 		}
176: 		return iEntry.stamp.Before(jEntry.stamp)
177: 	})
178: }
179: 
180: // evictExpired removes all entries whose TTL has expired and bumps the
181: // TTL eviction counter once per removed entry (issue #449). It returns
182: // the number of entries removed so the caller can dispatch the
183: // eviction observer after unlocking. Caller must hold c.mu.
184: func (c *SLMCache) evictExpired() int {
185: 	now := time.Now()
186: 	var keep []string
187: 	removed := 0
188: 	for _, key := range c.expiry {
189: 		entry, ok := c.entries[key]
190: 		if !ok {
191: 			continue // already removed
192: 		}
193: 		if now.Sub(entry.stamp) > c.ttl {
194: 			delete(c.entries, key)
195: 			removed++
196: 		} else {
197: 			keep = append(keep, key)
198: 		}
199: 	}
200: 	c.expiry = keep
201: 	c.sortExpiry()
202: 	if removed > 0 {
203: 		atomic.AddUint64(&c.ttlEvictions, uint64(removed))

205: 	return removed
206: }

208: // evictLru removes the least-recently-used (oldest by stamp) non-expired
209: // entry to make room for a new insertion and bumps the LRU eviction
210: // counter (issue #449). It returns 1 when an entry was removed, 0
211: // otherwise, so the caller can dispatch the eviction observer after
212: // unlocking. Caller must hold c.mu.
213: func (c *SLMCache) evictLru() int {
214: 	if len(c.expiry) == 0 {
215: 		return 0
216: 	}
217: 	// expiry is sorted by stamp, so the first element is the oldest.
218: 	lruKey := c.expiry[0]
219: 	delete(c.entries, lruKey)
220: 	c.expiry = c.expiry[1:]
221: 	atomic.AddUint64(&c.lruEvictions, 1)

225: // CacheHitKind describes the mechanism that produced a cache hit.
226: // It is returned as the third value from Get.
227: type CacheHitKind string
228: 
229: const (
230: 	// CacheHitExact means the prompt was found by exact string match.
231: 	CacheHitExact CacheHitKind = "exact"
232: 	// CacheHitSemantic means the prompt was found by cosine similarity
233: 	// against stored embeddings (issue #245).
234: 	CacheHitSemantic CacheHitKind = "semantic"
235: )

237: // Get returns the cached route for prompt and true if a non-expired
238: // entry exists; otherwise it returns the zero Route and false. On a
239: // miss the caller should invoke the SLM and then call Set to populate
240: // the cache.
241: //
242: // The returned string indicates how the hit was produced:
243: //   - CacheHitExact ("exact") for an exact string match (O(1))
244: //   - CacheHitSemantic ("semantic") for a cosine-similarity match
245: //   - "" (empty) when there is no hit
246: //
247: // When an Embedder is configured, Get first tries exact string matching
248: // (O(1), sub-millisecond). On an exact miss it falls back to semantic
249: // matching: it embeds the incoming prompt and scans stored embeddings
250: // for the best cosine similarity. If the best match exceeds the
251: // configured threshold the cached route is returned. Semantic matching
252: // requires an HTTP call to the embedder and may add latency.
253: func (c *SLMCache) Get(ctx context.Context, prompt string) (Route, bool, CacheHitKind) {
254: 	c.mu.RLock()
255: 	entry, ok := c.entries[prompt]
256: 	if ok && time.Since(entry.stamp) <= c.ttl {
257: 		route := entry.Route
258: 		c.mu.RUnlock()
259: 		return route, true, CacheHitExact
260: 	}
261: 	c.mu.RUnlock()
262: 
263: 	if c.embedder == nil {
264: 		return "", false, ""
265: 	}
266: 	return c.getSemantic(ctx, prompt)
267: }
268: 
269: // getSemantic embeds the prompt and finds the best cached embedding by
270: // cosine similarity. It returns the route of the best match if above
271: // the threshold, along with CacheHitSemantic; otherwise it returns
272: // "", false, "". Caller must not hold a lock (it releases the lock
273: // around the embedder call to avoid blocking Set during HTTP).
274: func (c *SLMCache) getSemantic(ctx context.Context, prompt string) (Route, bool, CacheHitKind) {
275: 	emb, err := c.embedder.Embed(ctx, prompt)
276: 	if err != nil {
277: 		atomic.AddUint64(&c.embedErrors, 1)
278: 		onEmbedErr := c.onEmbedError
279: 		// The lock is not held here (we are still in the read path before
280: 		// acquiring it), but we fire the callback synchronously after the
281: 		// embed call so it behaves consistently with Set.
282: 		if onEmbedErr != nil {
283: 			onEmbedErr()
284: 		}
285: 		return "", false, ""
286: 	}
287: 
288: 	c.mu.RLock()
289: 	defer c.mu.RUnlock()
290: 
291: 	var best Route
292: 	var bestScore float64 = -1
293: 
294: 	now := time.Now()
295: 	for _, entry := range c.entries {
296: 		if now.Sub(entry.stamp) > c.ttl {
297: 			continue
298: 		}
299: 		if entry.emb == nil {
300: 			continue
301: 		}
302: 		score := cosineSimilarity(emb, entry.emb)
303: 		if score > bestScore {
304: 			bestScore = score
305: 			best = entry.Route
306: 		}
307: 	}
308: 
309: 	if bestScore >= c.semThreshold {
310: 		return best, true, CacheHitSemantic
311: 	}
312: 	return "", false, ""
313: }

315: // Set records the routing decision for prompt. Subsequent calls to Get
316: // with the same prompt will return this decision until it expires.
317: // When an Embedder is configured Set also computes and stores the
318: // prompt embedding for semantic deduplication. Set is safe for
319: // concurrent use.
320: func (c *SLMCache) Set(ctx context.Context, prompt string, route Route) {
321: 	var ttlRemoved, lruRemoved int
322: 	var onEvict func(reason string)
323: 	var onEmbedErr func()
324: 
325: 	c.mu.Lock()
326: 
327: 	var emb []float64
328: 	if c.embedder != nil {
329: 		var err error
330: 		emb, err = c.embedder.Embed(ctx, prompt) // best-effort; embed errors are logged by caller
331: 		if err != nil {
332: 			atomic.AddUint64(&c.embedErrors, 1)
333: 			onEmbedErr = c.onEmbedError
334: 		}
335: 	}
336: 
337: 	// If at capacity, evict expired entries first, then LRU.
338: 	if c.maxEntries > 0 && len(c.entries) >= c.maxEntries {
339: 		ttlRemoved = c.evictExpired()
340: 		if len(c.entries) >= c.maxEntries {
341: 			lruRemoved = c.evictLru()
342: 		}
343: 	}
344: 
345: 	c.entries[prompt] = cachedDecision{
346: 		Route: route,
347: 		stamp: time.Now(),
348: 		emb:   emb,
349: 	}
350: 	c.expiry = append(c.expiry, prompt)
351: 
352: 	onEvict = c.onEviction
353: 	c.mu.Unlock()
354: 
355: 	// Dispatch the eviction observer AFTER releasing the cache lock
356: 	// so the observer can safely call into observability, logging,
357: 	// or any other subsystem (issue #449).
358: 	c.dispatchEvictions(onEvict, ttlRemoved, lruRemoved)
359: 
360: 	// Dispatch the embed-error observer (issue #741). The callback
361: 	// runs without holding the cache lock so it can safely call into
362: 	// observability or logging.
363: 	if onEmbedErr != nil {
364: 		onEmbedErr()
365: 	}
366: }

368: // SetEmbedding stores a routing decision with a pre-computed embedding.
369: // Use this when the caller has already computed the embedding to avoid
370: // redundant embedder calls (e.g. during cache warming).
371: func (c *SLMCache) SetEmbedding(prompt string, route Route, emb []float64) {
372: 	var ttlRemoved, lruRemoved int
373: 	var onEvict func(reason string)
374: 
375: 	c.mu.Lock()
376: 
377: 	if c.maxEntries > 0 && len(c.entries) >= c.maxEntries {
378: 		ttlRemoved = c.evictExpired()
379: 		if len(c.entries) >= c.maxEntries {
380: 			lruRemoved = c.evictLru()
381: 		}
382: 	}
383: 
384: 	c.entries[prompt] = cachedDecision{
385: 		Route: route,
386: 		stamp: time.Now(),
387: 		emb:   emb,
388: 	}
389: 	c.expiry = append(c.expiry, prompt)
390: 
391: 	onEvict = c.onEviction
392: 	c.mu.Unlock()
393: 
394: 	c.dispatchEvictions(onEvict, ttlRemoved, lruRemoved)

397: // dispatchEvictions fires the eviction observer once per removed
398: // entry. It runs without holding the cache lock so the observer is
399: // free to call into other subsystems. A nil observer is a no-op so
400: // the common path stays cheap.
401: func (c *SLMCache) dispatchEvictions(onEvict func(reason string), ttlRemoved, lruRemoved int) {
402: 	if onEvict == nil {
403: 		return
404: 	}
405: 	for i := 0; i < ttlRemoved; i++ {
406: 		onEvict(EvictionReasonTTL)
407: 	}
408: 	for i := 0; i < lruRemoved; i++ {
409: 		onEvict(EvictionReasonLRU)
410: 	}
411: }

413: // SetEvictionObserver registers a callback that is invoked once per
414: // evicted entry with reason = "ttl" or "lru" (issue #449). Pass nil
415: // to clear the observer. The callback runs on the goroutine that
416: // called Set/SetEmbedding, after the cache lock is released, so it
417: // must not be assumed to be on a dedicated worker. Callers that want
418: // to record into observability.RouteCounters should pass a closure
419: // that forwards to ObserveSLMCacheEviction; the closure will execute
420: // without re-entering the cache.
421: func (c *SLMCache) SetEvictionObserver(fn func(reason string)) {
422: 	c.mu.Lock()
423: 	c.onEviction = fn
424: 	c.mu.Unlock()
425: }

428: // embedder error inside Set or getSemantic (issue #741). Pass nil to
429: // clear the observer. The callback runs after the cache lock is
430: // released so it is safe to call into observability or logging.
431: // Callers that want to record into observability.RouteCounters should
432: // pass a closure that forwards to ObserveSLMCacheEmbedError.
433: func (c *SLMCache) SetEmbedErrorObserver(fn func()) {
434: 	c.mu.Lock()
435: 	c.onEmbedError = fn
436: 	c.mu.Unlock()

439: // SLMCacheStats holds state counters for the SLM cache. It is
440: // returned by Stats so callers can inspect cache effectiveness.
441: // TTLEvictions and LRUEvictions are cumulative since cache creation
442: // (issue #449) and reflect removals that actually happened; entries
443: // past TTL but not yet evicted are reflected by the Expired counter.
444: // EmbedErrors is the cumulative count of embedder errors (issue #741).

513: // router free of a rag import cycle. A zero vector on either side
514: // yields 0 so callers can sort without a special case.
515: func cosineSimilarity(a, b []float64) float64 {
516: 	n := len(a)
517: 	if len(b) < n {
518: 		n = len(b)

661: // ReadAllLimited reads from r with a byte limit of maxBytes. If the
662: // response body is larger than maxBytes, the body is truncated and
663: // ObserveResponseTruncated is called on rc (if non-nil) or the
664: // package-level counter is incremented (issue #365). This prevents
665: // memory exhaustion from a malicious upstream returning gigabytes.
666: // The returned error is any read error encountered before hitting the
667: // limit; a truncation itself is not treated as an error.
668: func ReadAllLimited(rc *RouteCounters, r io.Reader, maxBytes int) ([]byte, error) {
669: 	lr := io.LimitReader(r, int64(maxBytes))
670: 	body, err := io.ReadAll(lr)
671: 	// If we read exactly maxBytes, the response was likely truncated.
672: 	// The edge case of a response that is exactly maxBytes is
673: 	// astronomically unlikely at 64 MiB.
674: 	if len(body) >= maxBytes {
675: 		if rc != nil {
676: 			rc.ObserveResponseTruncated()
677: 		} else {
678: 			IncrementTruncationCounter()
679: 		}
680: 	}
681: 	return body, err
682: }

727: // Handler returns an http.Handler that writes the Prometheus text
728: // exposition. The handler sets Content-Type to the Prometheus text
729: // format and never errors — a scrape always returns 200 with the
730: // current counter snapshot. When a Collector is set (via SetCollector),
731: // counter/histogram families plus the collector's circuit-breaker
732: // gauges (issue #443) are merged into the output via RenderPrometheus.
733: func (rc *RouteCounters) Handler() http.Handler {
734: 	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
735: 		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8")
736: 		_, _ = rc.WriteTo(w)
737: 		if rc.collector != nil || len(rc.gaugeProviders) > 0 {
738: 			// *Collector satisfies GaugeProvider (issue #443), so its
739: 			// circuit-breaker state/failures/last-failure samples are
740: 			// merged into the gauge section alongside the explicit
741: 			// providers wired in main.go.
742: 			providers := rc.gaugeProviders
743: 			if rc.collector != nil {
744: 				providers = append(providers, rc.collector)
745: 			}
746: 			RenderPrometheus(w, rc.collector, providers...)
747: 		}
748: 	})
749: }

764: // Snapshot returns a point-in-time copy of the routing decision counters
765: // as a sorted slice. Used by the /status JSON endpoint to provide a
766: // routing distribution snapshot without exposing the internal counter map.
767: func (rc *RouteCounters) Snapshot() []RouteCounterEntry {
768: 	if rc == nil {
769: 		return nil
770: 	}
771: 	rc.mu.Lock()
772: 	defer rc.mu.Unlock()
773: 
774: 	var entries []RouteCounterEntry
775: 	for k, v := range rc.routeDecisions {
776: 		entries = append(entries, RouteCounterEntry{
777: 			Route:  k.route,
778: 			Source: k.source,
779: 			Count:  atomic.LoadUint64(v),
780: 		})
781: 	}
782: 	sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
783: 		if entries[i].Route != entries[j].Route {
784: 			return entries[i].Route < entries[j].Route
785: 		}
786: 		return entries[i].Source < entries[j].Source
787: 	})
788: 	return entries
789: }

964: // writeSeries emits one HELP line, one TYPE line, then one sample
965: // line per non-zero counter. The labels slice declares the label
966: // names in the order they should appear; the counterKey fields are
967: // read positionally via labelValue.
968: func writeSeries(w io.Writer, name, help string, m map[counterKey]*uint64, labels []string) (int64, error) {
969: 	var total int64
970: 	// Always emit HELP/TYPE so scrapers see the metric family even
971: 	// when no samples have been recorded yet.
972: 	n, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "# HELP %s %s\n# TYPE %s counter\n", name, help, name)
973: 	if err != nil {
974: 		return total + int64(n), err
975: 	}
976: 	total += int64(n)
977: 	if len(m) == 0 {
978: 		return total, nil
979: 	}
980: 	// Collect and sort keys for deterministic output.
981: 	keys := make([]counterKey, 0, len(m))
982: 	for k := range m {
983: 		keys = append(keys, k)
984: 	}

377: func TestCosineSimilarity(t *testing.T) {
378: 	tests := []struct {
379: 		name   string
380: 		a, b   []float64
381: 		want   float64
382: 		absTol float64
383: 	}{
384: 		{"identical", []float64{1, 0, 0}, []float64{1, 0, 0}, 1.0, 0.001},
385: 		{"orthogonal", []float64{1, 0, 0}, []float64{0, 1, 0}, 0.0, 0.001},
386: 		{"opposite", []float64{1, 0, 0}, []float64{-1, 0, 0}, -1.0, 0.001},
387: 		{"partial", []float64{1, 0, 0}, []float64{0.5, 0.5, 0}, 0.707, 0.01},
388: 		{"longer a", []float64{1, 0, 0, 0, 0}, []float64{1, 0, 0}, 1.0, 0.001},
389: 		{"longer b", []float64{1, 0, 0}, []float64{1, 0, 0, 0, 0}, 1.0, 0.001},
390: 		{"zero a", []float64{0, 0, 0}, []float64{1, 0, 0}, 0.0, 0.001},
391: 		{"zero b", []float64{1, 0, 0}, []float64{0, 0, 0}, 0.0, 0.001},
392: 	}
393: 	for _, tt := range tests {
394: 		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
395: 			got := cosineSimilarity(tt.a, tt.b)
396: 			if got < tt.want-tt.absTol || got > tt.want+tt.absTol {
397: 				t.Errorf("cosineSimilarity(%v, %v) = %v, want %v ± %v",
398: 					tt.a, tt.b, got, tt.want, tt.absTol)

576: func TestSLMCache_EvictionObserver(t *testing.T) {
577: 	// The eviction observer must fire once per removed entry with the
578: 	// correct reason. It must also fire AFTER the cache lock is
579: 	// released (we verify this indirectly by re-entering Set from
580: 	// inside the observer without deadlocking).

604: 		t.Errorf("first event = %q, want %q", events[0], EvictionReasonTTL)

606: 	if events[1] != EvictionReasonLRU {

627: func TestSLMCache_EvictionCounters_Concurrent(t *testing.T) {
628: 	// Run the race detector over the eviction paths: a stream of
629: 	// goroutines Set unique keys (so LRU pressure kicks in) while
630: 	// another stream calls Stats(). The eviction counters must end
631: 	// up consistent: every eviction either bumps TTL or LRU, never
632: 	// both, and Stats() must never race.
633: 	//
634: 	// Capacity is intentionally small (4) so LRU evictions happen
635: 	// quickly; keys are unique per iteration so the cache churns.
636: 	c := NewSLMCache(time.Hour, 4)
637: 	ctx := context.Background()
638: 
639: 	var writers sync.WaitGroup
640: 	var readers sync.WaitGroup
641: 	const goroutines = 8
642: 	const iterations = 200
643:

1. **`SLMCache` changes** (`internal/router/slm_cache.go`):

   - Modify `getSemantic` to trigger proactive eviction when `Stale() > maxStale`
   - Add `TryEvictExpired()` method that acquires a write lock briefly to evict expired entries (non-blocking, safe to call from within RLock)

2. **Config changes** (`internal/config/config.go` and `internal/config/yaml.go`):
   - Add `SLMCacheMaxStale int` config field and corresponding `NEXUS_SLMCACHE_MAX_STALE` env var
   - Wire it into `NewSLMCache` or add a `SetMaxStale` method

3. **Metrics changes** (`internal/observability/routemetrics.go`):
   - Add `nexus_slm_cache_stale_entries` gauge

4. **Tests**

The key insight is that `getSemantic` holds an RLock but can't call `evictExpired` which needs a write lock. The solution is a `TryEvictExpired()` method that uses a short-lived write lock for eviction, called asynchronously from `getSemantic` when stale entries exceed the threshold.

Since this is Go with sync.RWMutex, readers don't block each other but writers block everyone. The approach is to check if `maxStale > 0` and `stale > maxStale` under RLock, then spawn a goroutine that acquires a write lock briefly to evict. This avoids blocking the semantic scan, prevents unbounded stale entry growth, and introduces minimal overhead on the hot path.

For `Get()` which doesn't use `getSemantic`, expired entries still accumulate since it only checks exact matches under RLock and skips to `getSemantic` for semantic matching. The solution is to trigger proactive eviction in `getSemantic` itself—when stale entries exceed `maxStale`, a background goroutine performs the eviction. If `Get()` never calls `getSemantic` with an embedder, stale entries won't be evicted, but that's acceptable since the issue specifically targets `getSemantic`'s accumulation problem.

The real concern is low request volume and long TTL scenarios where `Set()` isn't called frequently enough to trigger the normal eviction logic. Wait, there's a problem. The stale count is done under RLock, but then the lock is released before we check `stale > c.maxStale`. But `c.maxStale` was read under RLock, so that's fine. However, there's a race: between releasing the RLock and spawning the goroutine, another goroutine could change `c.maxStale`. But this is fine because:
1. We read `maxStale` under RLock
2. We release RLock
3. We check `stale > maxStale` (where `maxStale` is a local copy)
4. If true, we spawn a goroutine with the local `stale` value captured in the closure


This is actually correct behavior - if stale is 5 and maxStale is 1, we'll trigger eviction even if maxStale changes to 1000 right after releasing the lock. # per call. Decisions are near-deterministic (temperature 0.1), so
# identical prompts hit the cache. Key is SHA256(prompt). LRU + TTL.
# Max entries caps memory; set to 0 to disable the cache entirely.
NEXUS_SLM_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=512
# TTL for SLM routing decision cache entries. Set to 0 to disable expiry
# (pure LRU eviction only). Default 30s keeps decisions fresh while
# still absorbing bursts of identical prompts.
NEXUS_SLM_CACHE_TTL=30s
# Cosine similarity floor for semantic cache hits in the SLM decision
# cache (issue #245). When > 0, prompts with similar intent but different
# wording share cached route decisions. 0.0 disables semantic dedup
# (exact SHA256 match only). Range [0.0-1.0]; out-of-range values
# are clamped.
NEXUS_SLMCACHE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD=0.0
# Hard-escalation threshold for SLM confidence (issue #301). When the
# SLM returns local/fusion with confidence below this value, the
# planner overrides to frontier. Default 0.3 is deliberately conservative:
# it only fires when the SLM is quite uncertain, preserving local-route
# savings for clear-cut cases. Set to 0 to disable the hard override
# (soft bias via ConfidenceStore still applies when wired).

# per call. Decisions are near-deterministic (temperature 0.1), so
# identical prompts hit the cache. Key is SHA256(prompt). LRU + TTL.
# Max entries caps memory; set to 0 to disable the cache entirely.
NEXUS_SLM_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=512
# TTL for SLM routing decision cache entries. Set to 0 to disable expiry
# (pure LRU eviction only). Default 30s keeps decisions fresh while
# still absorbing bursts of identical prompts.
NEXUS_SLM_CACHE_TTL=30s
# Cosine similarity floor for semantic cache hits in the SLM decision
# cache (issue #245). When > 0, prompts with similar intent but different
# wording share cached route decisions. 0.0 disables semantic dedup
# (exact SHA256 match only). Range [0.0-1.0]; out-of-range values
# are clamped.
NEXUS_SLMCACHE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD=0.0
# Hard-escalation threshold for SLM confidence (issue #301). When the
# SLM returns local/fusion with confidence below this value, the
# planner overrides to frontier. Default 0.3 is deliberately conservative:
# it only fires when the SLM is quite uncertain, preserving local-route
# savings for clear-cut cases. Set to 0 to disable the hard override
# (soft bias via ConfidenceStore still applies when wired).

parts.text: All done! Let me provide a summary of what was done.

**PR #859 created successfully.**

### Summary

**Files changed (7):**

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `internal/router/slm_cache.go` | Added `maxStale` field, `Stale()`, `SetMaxStale()`, `EvictExpired()`; modified `getSemantic` to spawn background eviction when `stale > maxStale` |
| `internal/router/slm_cache_test.go` | Added 9 new tests for stale entry tracking and proactive eviction |
| `internal/config/config.go` | Added `SLMCacheMaxStale` field + `NEXUS_SLMCACHE_MAX_STALE` env var parsing |
| `internal/config/yaml.go` | Added `SLMCacheMaxStale` YAML field + env override + default |
| `cmd/nexus/main.go` | Wired `SetMaxStale()` on cache creation; added `nexus_slm_cache_stale_entries` to `/metrics` gauge |
| `internal/observability/prometheus.go` | Added `nexus_slm_cache_stale_entries` gauge metadata |
| `.env.example` | Documented `NEXUS_SLMCACHE_MAX_STALE` |

**Key design decisions:**
- `Stale()` counts expired-but-not-yet-evicted entries under RLock (same logic as `Stats().Expired`)
- `EvictExpired()` is public for background use, acquires Lock briefly, fires eviction observer after release
- `getSemantic` checks `maxStale > 0 && stale > maxStale` after its scan, spawns a fire-and-forget goroutine — never blocks the read path
- `nexus_slm_cache_stale_entries` gauge reflects live `Stale()` count at scrape time
- `NEXUS_SLMCACHE_MAX_STALE=0` (default) disables proactive eviction (backward compatible)
